newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Cera Bank buys Swiss Inca Bank.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Cera Bank buys Swiss Inca Bank.

text.p: Belgian Cera Bank said on Friday it bought 100 percent of the shares in Inca Bank SA, a Swiss bank specialising in private banking.
Cera Bank said in a statement it signed the purchase agreement on June 4.
Inca Bank, based in Geneva and with a representative office in Zurich, will be renamed Cera Bank (Suisse) SA/Cera Bank (Schweiz) AG from July 1.
Cera said all units active in private banking, such as Cerabank Luxembourg, and brokers Nedee & Co and Nedee Luxembourg, would be given stakes in the capital of Inca Bank in the near future.
A Cera spokesman declined to give the purchase price. "That is not usual," he said.
Inca fitted in with Cera's strategy, which was to start developing private banking in Switzerland. Inca would act as a base for that, he said.
Cera has been expanding actively recently. It plans finalise the takeover of Banque Indosuez Belgium next week.
In the autumn it plans to open its first office in the Netherlands, in the border town of Maastricht.

Unlisted Cera, Belgium's sixth-largest bank with 1996 net consolidated profit of 5.78 billion francs and a balance sheet total of 1,304 billion francs, had said in March it was planning an acquisition in Switzerland before the summer.
Cera said at the time it would open additional branches in the Netherlands if Maastricht met its expectations.
The bank employs 4,573 people and has 939 offices. It has subsidiaries in Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the U.S.
Its return on equity rose to 8.30 in 1996 from 6.08 in 1995 and 5.76 in 1994. Profits in the past five years more than doubled.
